title: Render Pocket's list
prompt:
Write the body of `renderExpenses(expenses)` so it rebuilds the page from the data:

1. Clear `#expense-list`.
2. Append one `<li>` per expense with the text `Coffee: $4.50` (label, colon, formatted amount), its `data-id` set to the expense's `id`, and the class `big` when the amount is 10000 cents or more.
3. Set `#total` to `Total: ` followed by the formatted sum.

Calling `renderExpenses` again must replace the list, not add to it, and labels must be shown as plain text.
hints: Select the two containers once at the top: `document.querySelector("#expense-list")` and `document.querySelector("#total")`.
For each expense: `document.createElement("li")`, set `textContent`, set `li.dataset.id`, maybe `li.classList.add("big")`, then `list.append(li)`.
Start the function with `list.replaceChildren();` so a second render does not duplicate items, and compute the total with `reduce`.
explanation: The render function is the single place that decides what the list looks like. Clearing first with `replaceChildren()` means calling it again, after the data changes, produces exactly one item per expense instead of appending duplicates. `textContent` puts the label in as plain text, so a label like `Tea` is shown literally instead of becoming bold (or, with nastier input, running code). The `big` class only flags the item; the stylesheet decides how flagged items look. `dataset.id` writes a `data-id` attribute you will use in the next lesson to know which expense a click belongs to.

checks.data-id: Each item has its expense id in data-id
checks.big-class: Only expenses of 10000 cents or more get the class "big"
checks.rerender: Rendering again replaces the list and shows labels as plain text
